{{Short description|Proven conjecture in probability theory}}
{{Distinguish|text=the [[spectral gap conjecture]]}}

In [[probability theory]], '''Aldous' spectral gap conjecture''' is the statement that two [[Markov chain]]s associated to a graph, namely the [[random walk]] and the interchange process, have the same [[spectral gap]]. The conjecture was proven in 2009 by Caputo, Liggett, and Richthammer.<ref name="x999">{{cite journal | last1=Caputo | first1=Pietro | last2=Liggett | first2=Thomas | last3=Richthammer | first3=Thomas | title=Proof of Aldous' spectral gap conjecture | journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society | volume=23 | issue=3 | date=2010-01-26 | issn=0894-0347 | doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-10-00659-4 | pages=831–851 | url=https://www.ams.org/jams/2010-23-03/S0894-0347-10-00659-4/ | arxiv=0906.1238 }}</ref>

== History ==
The statement was proven for the [[complete graph]] by [[Persi Diaconis]] and Mehrdad Shahshahani in 1981,<ref name="n395">{{cite journal | last1=Diaconis | first1=Persi | last2=Shahshahani | first2=Mehrdad | title=Generating a random permutation with random transpositions | journal=Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und Verwandte Gebiete | volume=57 | issue=2 | date=1981 | issn=0044-3719 | doi=10.1007/BF00535487 | pages=159–179 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00535487 }}</ref> and for [[star graph]]s by Leopold Flatto, [[Andrew Odlyzko]], and David Wales in 1985.<ref name="m794">{{cite journal | last1=Flatto | first1=L. | last2=Odlyzko | first2=A. M. | last3=Wales | first3=D. B. | title=Random Shuffles and Group Representations | journal=The Annals of Probability | volume=13 | issue=1 | date=1985-02-01 | issn=0091-1798 | doi=10.1214/aop/1176993073 | url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-probability/volume-13/issue-1/Random-Shuffles-and-Group-Representations/10.1214/aop/1176993073.full | page=}}</ref> It was first formally stated as an open problem in a book in preparation by [[David Aldous]] and James Fill.<ref name="r959">{{cite web | title=Aldous-Fill book | website=Sitemap for www.stat.berkeley.edu | date=1999-07-20 | url=https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html }}</ref>

For weighted trees, the statement was proven in 1996 by Shirin Handjani and Douglas Jungreis.<ref name="d561">{{cite journal | last1=Handjani | first1=Shirin | last2=Jungreis | first2=Douglas | title=Rate of convergence for shuffling cards by transpositions | journal=Journal of Theoretical Probability | volume=9 | issue=4 | date=1996 | issn=0894-9840 | doi=10.1007/BF02214260 | pages=983–993 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02214260 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> For boxes in <math>\mathbb{Z}^{d}</math>, the statement was independently proven by Morris and by Conomos and Starr in 2008.<ref name="p369">{{cite journal | last=Morris | first=Ben | title=Spectral gap for the interchange process in a box | journal=Electronic Communications in Probability | volume=13 | issue=none | date=2008-01-01 | issn=1083-589X | doi=10.1214/ECP.v13-1381 | url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/electronic-communications-in-probability/volume-13/issue-none/Spectral-gap-for-the-interchange-process-in-a-box/10.1214/ECP.v13-1381.full | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="o837">{{cite journal | last1=Starr | first1=Shannon | last2=Conomos | first2=Matthew P | title=Asymptotics of the spectral gap for the interchange process on large hypercubes | journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=2011 | issue=10 | date=2011-10-20 | issn=1742-5468 | doi=10.1088/1742-5468/2011/10/p10018 | arxiv=0802.1368 }}</ref> The full connector was proven in 2009.<ref name="x999"/>
